assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Reliance Industries (consolidated, Rs crore). Five reported segments on the company basis (gross revenue = value of sales and services incl. GST; EBITDA = company definition) plus a negative line for GST, excise duty and inter-segment sales (zero margin, PLAYBOOK §7) so that revenue ties to Screener. Company EBITDA includes other income (mostly treasury income in Others); `unallocated` removes it so model EBITDA is on Screener's basis, and `otherIncome` adds it back below EBITDA. History is attributable to RIL shareholders (RELIANCE.patch.js); the tax line also carries minorities.

segments.name: Oil to Chemicals (O2C)
segments._why: Revenue tracks crude: Brent averaged $104.5/bbl in Q1FY27 (Q1FY26 ~$68) and O2C revenue rose 30%; we assume ~$95 for FY27 (Hormuz still disrupted at 30-Sep, Brent ~$100-107 in September) and ~$80 in FY28-29: +22%, -8%, +3%. EBITDA Rs60,546 cr in FY26 (9.1%); Q1FY27 Rs17,010 cr (8.4%) despite a planned turnaround, export duties/SAED, PSU under-recoveries and record crude premiums and freight. FY27E ~Rs68K cr (Q1 run-rate), FY28E ~Rs66K cr as cracks normalise, FY29E ~Rs68K cr (8.9%). Street: Emkay Jun-28E O2C EBITDA Rs67.7K cr; MOSL FY28E O2C+E&P Rs80.4K cr.

segments.name: Oil and Gas (E&P)
segments._why: KG-D6 gas fell from 26.6 to 24.8 MMSCMD in a year (natural decline) at a capped $8.9/MMBtu for H1FY27; liquids earn $107/bbl. FY27E +2.7% on oil prices, then -6% a year as volumes decline and oil normalises; margin 79% (Q1FY27) easing to 76%. EBITDA ~Rs19.4K / 17.7K / 16.4K cr. Street: Emkay Jun-28E Rs14.0K cr, BOBCAPS Rs19.0K cr.

segments.name: Digital Services (Jio)
segments._why: Gross revenue (value of services). FY26 +14%; Q1FY27 JPL gross +12% with ARPU Rs215.6 (+Rs7 YoY) and no tariff increase in 12 months; subscribers 533 mn, FWA 14 mn. FY27E +12% (no tariff rise assumed before FY28); FY28E +14% on a ~10% effective tariff increase (street assumes ~15%; Jefferies moved its assumed hike to Dec-2026), FY29E +11%. EBITDA margin on gross revenue 43.5% in FY26, ~46% in Q1FY27 (JPL 53.3% on operating revenue): 44.5% / 45.5% / 46%. Sep-28E EBITDA ~Rs1.08 lakh cr vs MOSL RJio Rs1.04 lakh cr, BOBCAPS Jun-28E Rs85K cr.

segments.name: Retail (RRVL)
segments._why: FY26 gross Rs3,71,085 cr includes the consumer-brands business until its demerger on 1-Dec-2025. Q1FY27 +7.4% reported, +11.6% like-for-like. FY27E +7.8% reported (~+12% underlying), FY28-29E +14% as online scale builds. EBITDA margin on gross 7.3% in FY26, 7.0% in Q1FY27 (hyper-local investment): 6.9% / 7.2% / 7.7%: EBITDA +2% / +19% / +22%, ~1.5x in three years vs management's 2x objective (FY27-29). Street Sep/Jun-28E: MOSL Rs31.8K cr, BOBCAPS Rs34.6K cr, Emkay ~Rs35.7K cr (100%).

segments.name: Others (media, consumer brands, treasury, unallocated)
segments._why: JioStar (FY26 revenue Rs34,917 cr), RCPL (Q1FY27 Rs8,600 cr, 2.1x), other businesses, treasury income and unallocable costs. Revenue +35% in FY27E (RCPL now outside Retail and doubling), then +20%, +15%. EBITDA incl. treasury income: FY26 Rs15,797 cr ex the Rs8,924 cr Asian Paints gain; Q1FY27 Rs4,520 cr. 16.6% / 17% / 17% = Rs18.0K / 22.2K / 25.5K cr. Valued in the SOTP on broker and transaction values, not on this EBITDA.

segments.name: GST, excise and inter-segment sales
segments._why: Screener revenue = gross segment revenue less GST, excise duty and inter-segment sales: 19.3% of gross in FY25, 19.65% in FY26. Held at 19.65%; growth synced by RELIANCE.sync.js to the gross total.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Other income inside company EBITDA (removed to reach Screener EBITDA, added back in otherIncome)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Company EBITDA = Screener operating profit + other income (FY26: 1,79,065 + 28,846 = 2,07,911). Same values as otherIncome.
assumptions._esopWhy: No separate share-based cost line; zero (keeps the Excel segment model working).
assumptions._capexWhy: Capex Rs1,44,271 cr in FY26 (segment note) and Rs38,682 cr in Q1FY27 (new energy, hyper-local retail, O2C projects, data centres); management gives no number but keeps capex within operating cash flow and net debt/EBITDA below 1x. We model Rs1.45 / 1.40 / 1.30 lakh cr as 5G spending is done and new energy peaks.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs57,688 cr = 3.94% of average gross block; Q1FY27 Rs15,100 cr (5G assets capitalised). The engine depreciates capex at once while CWIP (Rs2.38 lakh cr) is held flat, so we use 3.75%: FY27E ~Rs61K cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt on the engine's basis, so no yield on treasury; other income is built in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built: interest and gains on ~Rs2.5 lakh cr of cash and marketable securities (~7% = ~Rs17.5K cr) + income on the Rs98,881 cr JDFPL preference shares and other investments + share of JVs/associates (FY26 Rs144 cr). FY26 Rs28,846 cr incl. the Rs8,924 cr Asian Paints gain = Rs19,922 cr recurring; TTM to Jun-26 Rs20,393 cr; Q1FY27 Rs6,550 cr (treasury gains). FY27E Rs23K cr (Q1 run-rate tempered), FY28-29E Rs21K cr as cash funds capex.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs27,061 cr; Q1FY27 Rs8,337 cr (+18.5% YoY) as interest on 5G spectrum and network is no longer capitalised. FY27E Rs33.5K cr, easing slowly. Jio IPO proceeds (up to Rs27,500 cr to repay RJIL debt) are not in the base: the issue was not priced by 30-Sep.
assumptions._taxWhy: This line is tax PLUS minority interests, as % of PBT (no minority line in the engine; profit is attributable). Tax 25% of PBT (Q1FY27 24.9%). Minorities 13% / 14% / 14.5% of PAT: FY26 Rs14,979 cr = 15.6% of PAT, Q1FY27 Rs2,250 cr = 9.7% (RCPL/JioStar losses shared); Jio (33.57% outside) grows fastest. Combined: 1 - 0.75 x (1 - m).
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs6/share = 10% of EPS (FY25 Rs5.50).

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at one rate; beta 0.75 gives 11.0%, our WACC (Ke ~12% on ~88% equity at market, after-tax debt ~6.5% on ~12%).
dcf._tgWhy: Nominal India growth with mature refining: 5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades to 7% (consumer and digital outgrow O2C).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Screener-basis margin ~16-17% in FY27-29E stays ~17% as Jio and Retail gain weight against low-margin O2C revenue.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~11% of revenue now fades to 7% (new energy and 5G build-outs done).

cover.headline: Good businesses, fair price: our numbers match the street, its multiples do not match the market
cover.lead: Reliance is four businesses in one stock: refining and petrochemicals (O2C), Jio, Reliance Retail and a pre-revenue New Energy build-out, with gas fields, JioStar and consumer brands on the side. Q1FY27 was a record (EBITDA ₹54,067 cr, +10%) because the Iran war lifted fuel cracks, while Retail stalled and Jio kept compounding. We forecast EPS of ₹60.8 / ₹67.6 / ₹76.5 for FY27-29E, close to the street. The street values RIL on a **sum of the parts** and so do we, but with each segment priced like its listed peers on the house rule: **O2C 3.5x, Jio 7x, Retail 22.5x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA** (E&P 5x, the brokers' median), New Energy at cost, less net debt, spectrum dues and minorities: **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). We initiate with HOLD.** Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}. At the street's own multiples our numbers give ₹1,766, which is where the street's median target (₹1,685) sits: the gap is the multiple, not the earnings.

arguments.h: O2C: a war windfall that the state shares
arguments.p: Q1FY27 O2C EBITDA ₹17,010 cr (+17%) on diesel and jet cracks of ~$63/bbl, but export duties, PSU under-recoveries, $20/bbl crude premiums and 10x freight took much of it. We model ₹67,883 cr in FY27E falling to ₹66,170 cr in FY28E. Listed refiners have traded at a median 3.9x forward EBITDA since 2021 and sit 14% below their own history now (EV/EBITDA): hence 3.5x, half the street's ~7x.

arguments.h: Jio: the IPO will set the price we cannot
arguments.p: Q1FY27 EBITDA ₹20,865 cr (+15%), 53.3% margin, 533 mn subscribers, without a tariff rise. The DRHP is filed and SEBI cleared it on 28-Aug-2026; media talk of ~US$130-137 bn. Bharti Airtel has traded at 7.8x forward EBITDA since 2021 (telecom set 7.8x, −8% now): we use 7x on Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹1,08,594 cr; the street uses 11.5-12x.

arguments.h: Retail: growth slowed, the spend went up
arguments.p: Q1FY27 gross revenue +7.4% (+11.6% like-for-like) and EBITDA −1% as stores turn into dark stores for 30-minute delivery. Management targets 2x EBITDA over FY27-29; we model ~1.5x. Listed retailers traded at a median 35.1x forward EBITDA since 2021 but sit 36% below their own history now: 22.5x vs the street's 27-35x.

At ₹1,187 the stock trades at 16.5x Sep-28E EPS, against its own forward median of 22.7x since 2021 (P/E value ₹1,621). Our DCF (no working-capital release) gives ₹950. Three methods, three answers, the target in the middle: we would buy below ₹1,045.

catalysts: Jio Platforms IPO: price band and dates (media expected late October to around Diwali); the listing price re-marks a third of our SOTP.
Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): O2C margin under export duties; Retail growth against the 2x EBITDA plan.
A mobile tariff increase (street assumes ~15% in FY27-28; none in our FY27E).
Strait of Hormuz: a durable ceasefire would cut fuel cracks; fortnightly export-duty reviews (diesel ₹20/l from 16-Sep-2026).
New Energy: 40 GWh battery line commissioning this year, power from Kutch, partners for the rest of the green-fuel capacity after the US$3 bn Samsung C&T ammonia contract.

blocks.p: Three corporate actions matter for reading the numbers. **The 1:1 bonus (Oct-2024)** doubled the share count to 1,353.2 cr; Screener and we show all history on the new count. **The Asian Paints sale (Q1FY26)** put a ₹8,924 cr gain into FY26 EBITDA and other income (₹7,371 cr after tax); FY26 EPS of ₹59.69 is ~₹54 without it. **The consumer-brands demerger (1-Dec-2025)** moved Campa, Independence and the other brands from Retail to a new RIL subsidiary (RCPL, same 83.56% ownership), so Retail's reported growth from Q4FY26 understates the like-for-like (Q1FY27: +7.4% reported, +11.6% adjusted).

blocks.callout: **The Jio IPO (pending at 30-Sep-2026):** a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, no offer for sale, up to ₹27,500 cr to repay Jio's debt. RIL's 66.43% would fall by ~2 points (27 cr shares are ~2.9% of the enlarged equity, per Bloomberg/TNW); RIL shareholders get a reserved quota, not cash. SEBI issued its observations on 28-Aug-2026; the price band was not announced by our as-of date.

sections.title: A war-time oil market, a three-player telecom market, and retail moving online

blocks.h: Oil and refining: the Hormuz shock

blocks.p: The US-Iran war (from 28-Feb-2026) and repeated closures of the Strait of Hormuz shut in >10 mb/d of Middle East oil and ~300 mcm/d of LNG for over 100 days (CFR, 8-Jul-2026). Brent peaked at $144/bbl intraday and averaged $104.5 in Q1FY27; ME refining (3 mb/d) and ethylene (~30 MMT) capacity was hit; diesel/ATF cracks reached ~$63/bbl. A US-Iran ceasefire announcement eased prices at quarter-end, but strikes resumed from 30-Aug and Brent was ~$100-107 in September. Global oil demand fell 4.8 mb/d YoY in Q1FY27; RIL expects -1 mb/d in CY2026 and +2 mb/d in CY2027.

India froze pump prices (since Apr-2022) and cut excise ₹10/l (27-Mar-2026); PSU marketers absorbed ~₹1 lakh cr of under-recoveries in ~10 weeks (Mar-May 2026) and raised prices ₹3/l on 15-May-2026. Export duties/SAED on diesel and ATF from 26-Mar-2026 (diesel peaked at ₹55.5/l on 11-Apr; ₹20/l from 16-Sep-2026), reviewed fortnightly. US sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil (22-Oct-2025) ended RIL's Russian crude at its export refinery from 20-Nov-2025; 2026 waivers allowed some cargoes until 17-Jun-2026.

Three private operators; Jio 533 mn subscribers (Q1FY27), ARPU ₹215.6 with no tariff increase in the last 12 months (Q1FY27 call); street expects ~10-15% in FY27-28. Jio has >78% of fixed-wireless (FWA) share.

Quick commerce (Blinkit, Instamart, Zepto) is pulling grocery and electronics online; RRVL responds with hyper-local delivery from stores (JioMart orders +116% YoY in Q1FY27) at a margin cost. Listed retailers de-rated ~30% vs five-year medians by 30-Sep-2026.

blocks.callout: **So what:** RIL's FY27 profits are being made in an abnormal oil market. The cracks that drove Q1 depend on how long Middle East supply stays disrupted, and the government is taking a share through export duties that it reviews every fortnight. We treat FY27 O2C earnings as above-normal and fade them in FY28.

sections.title: O2C: record cracks, but the state, the shippers and the sellers of crude took a large share

blocks.p: O2C is RIL's biggest business by revenue (₹6,62,401 cr in FY26, ~half of gross segment revenue) and its most volatile by profit. EBITDA fell from ₹62,393 cr in FY24 to ₹54,988 cr in FY25 as cracks normalised, recovered to ₹60,546 cr in FY26, and Q1FY27 made ₹17,010 cr (+17% YoY), a four-year high, even with a planned crude-unit and coker shutdown (throughput 18.1 vs 19.1 MMT). Fuel cracks 2.6-4.4x a year earlier (gasoline $35.4, gasoil $62.9, ATF $63.0/bbl); PE delta +46%, polyester chain +17%; weighed down by SAED/export duties, under-recoveries on domestic fuel sales and sales to PSUs, crude premiums up to ~$20/bbl, freight ~10x, planned CDU and coker turnaround (volumes -10%).

blocks.p: **JioStar** (Viacom18 merged with Disney's Star India in Nov-2024; RIL's economic interest ~49%, Disney 36.84%) had FY26 revenue ₹34,917 cr and net profit ₹3,434 cr; Q1FY27 revenue ₹10,946 cr (+14%) and EBITDA ₹1,049 cr, with ~530 mn monthly JioHotstar users. The merger valued it at ₹70,352 cr; we use that value (₹26 a share for RIL's share).

**Reliance Consumer Products** (Campa, Independence and other brands, demerged from Retail in Dec-2025) grew 2.1x to ₹8,600 cr of Q1FY27 sales (Campa ~₹2,900 cr, Independence ~₹3,200 cr), >80% through outside channels, while spending heavily on advertising (IPL's #1 TV advertiser). We use Motilal Oswal's ₹52,900 cr (2x FY28E sales, RIL share; ₹39 a share), the only broker value we found.

**New Energy:** ~1 GWp of heterojunction modules produced, scaling to 20 GWp; a 40 GWh battery line due this year (120 GWh planned); Kutch solar-plus-storage installation to start after the monsoon; a US$3 bn green-ammonia supply deal with Samsung C&T. No revenue yet. We carry it at the ₹75,000 cr the street uses as committed capital (1.0x, ₹55 a share); BOBCAPS also uses 1.0x, Emkay and PL 2.0x, Morgan Stanley ~US$20 bn.

sections.title: Twice the EBITDA of FY21, but profit per share has grown only ~9% a year

blocks.p: Revenue more than doubled from FY21 (₹4.66 lakh cr, Screener basis) to FY26 (₹10.56 lakh cr), mostly because crude prices recovered. The quality of the growth is in EBITDA: company EBITDA rose from ₹97,580 cr to ₹2,07,911 cr, with Jio (₹34,035 cr to ₹76,560 cr) and Retail (₹9,842 cr to ₹27,034 cr) doing most of the work and O2C up 1.6x. But shareholders saw less of it: depreciation doubled (₹26,572 cr to ₹57,688 cr), interest rose as 5G and new projects were capitalised, and outside investors in Jio and Retail now take ~₹15,000 cr a year. EPS (after the 2024 bonus) went from ₹38.75 to ₹59.69 (FY26 includes ~₹5.4 of Asian Paints gain): ~9% a year.

sections.title: The street: 14 of 14 post-Q1 notes positive, median target ₹1,685

blocks.p: After the Q1FY27 results (17-Jul-2026) 14 houses we could trace kept positive ratings, with targets from ₹1,510 (Macquarie) to ₹1,870 (Goldman Sachs): median ₹1,685, +42% from the 30-Sep-2026 close of ₹1,187. FactSet's mean was ₹1,682 across 31 analysts (20-Jul). Every house that discloses its method uses a **sum of the parts: O2C at 6-7.5x EV/EBITDA, E&P 4.5-6x, Jio 11.5-12x, Retail 27-35x, New Energy at 1-2x committed capital**; Motilal Oswal also takes 25% off the Jio stake as a holding-company discount. The stock fell from ₹1,327 on results day to ₹1,187 (−11%), and ~26% from its ₹1,612 high of 5-Jan-2026, while targets were not cut: the press blamed export levies, Middle East volatility, high capex and weak free-cash conversion, and the primary-only Jio IPO.

blocks.p: **What you buy:** India's best telecom franchise, its largest retailer and a world-scale refinery, plus options on media, consumer brands and clean energy, run by a management that executes. **What you pay:** ₹1,187, 16.5x Sep-28E EPS, a −27% discount to its own forward P/E history, but roughly what the parts are worth if each is priced like its listed peers are priced today. **Why not a BUY:** the street's ₹1,685 needs Jio at 12x, Retail at ~30x and O2C at ~7x when Bharti, the listed retailers and the refiners have all de-rated; and the group still turns record EBITDA into thin free cash flow. **Why not a SELL:** our earnings are in line with the street, the balance sheet is strong, and the Jio IPO could re-price the largest part. **How we would act:** HOLD at {{dcf.tp|inr}}; we would buy below ₹1,045 and sell above ₹1,265, and we will revisit when the Jio IPO is priced.

EBITDA incl. treasury income: FY26 Rs15,797 cr ex the Rs8,924 cr Asian Paints gain; Q1FY27 Rs4,520 cr. 16.6% / 17% / 17% = Rs18.0K / 22.2K / 25.5K cr. Valued in the SOTP on broker and transaction values, not on this EBITDA.

segments.name: GST, excise and inter-segment sales
segments._why: Screener revenue = gross segment revenue less GST, excise duty and inter-segment sales: 19.3% of gross in FY25, 19.65% in FY26. Held at 19.65%; growth synced by RELIANCE.sync.js to the gross total.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Other income inside company EBITDA (removed to reach Screener EBITDA, added back in otherIncome)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Company EBITDA = Screener operating profit + other income (FY26: 1,79,065 + 28,846 = 2,07,911). Same values as otherIncome.
assumptions._esopWhy: No separate share-based cost line; zero (keeps the Excel segment model working).
assumptions._capexWhy: Capex Rs1,44,271 cr in FY26 (segment note) and Rs38,682 cr in Q1FY27 (new energy, hyper-local retail, O2C projects, data centres); management gives no number but keeps capex within operating cash flow and net debt/EBITDA below 1x. We model Rs1.45 / 1.40 / 1.30 lakh cr as 5G spending is done and new energy peaks.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs57,688 cr = 3.94% of average gross block; Q1FY27 Rs15,100 cr (5G assets capitalised). The engine depreciates capex at once while CWIP (Rs2.38 lakh cr) is held flat, so we use 3.75%: FY27E ~Rs61K cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt on the engine's basis, so no yield on treasury; other income is built in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built: interest and gains on ~Rs2.5 lakh cr of cash and marketable securities (~7% = ~Rs17.5K cr) + income on the Rs98,881 cr JDFPL preference shares and other investments + share of JVs/associates (FY26 Rs144 cr). FY26 Rs28,846 cr incl. the Rs8,924 cr Asian Paints gain = Rs19,922 cr recurring; TTM to Jun-26 Rs20,393 cr; Q1FY27 Rs6,550 cr (treasury gains). FY27E Rs23K cr (Q1 run-rate tempered), FY28-29E Rs21K cr as cash funds capex.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs27,061 cr; Q1FY27 Rs8,337 cr (+18.5% YoY) as interest on 5G spectrum and network is no longer capitalised. FY27E Rs33.5K cr, easing slowly. Jio IPO proceeds (up to Rs27,500 cr to repay RJIL debt) are not in the base: the issue was not priced by 30-Sep.
assumptions._taxWhy: This line is tax PLUS minority interests, as % of PBT (no minority line in the engine; profit is attributable). Tax 25% of PBT (Q1FY27 24.9%). Minorities 13% / 14% / 14.5% of PAT: FY26 Rs14,979 cr = 15.6% of PAT, Q1FY27 Rs2,250 cr = 9.7% (RCPL/JioStar losses shared); Jio (33.57% outside) grows fastest. Combined: 1 - 0.75 x (1 - m).
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs6/share = 10% of EPS (FY25 Rs5.50).

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at one rate; beta 0.75 gives 11.0%, our WACC (Ke ~12% on ~88% equity at market, after-tax debt ~6.5% on ~12%).
dcf._tgWhy: Nominal India growth with mature refining: 5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades to 7% (consumer and digital outgrow O2C).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Screener-basis margin ~16-17% in FY27-29E stays ~17% as Jio and Retail gain weight against low-margin O2C revenue.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~11% of revenue now fades to 7% (new energy and 5G build-outs done).
